_comment: AI players (Homestead's own). The AI knows the whole map. Every thinkSeconds it starts at most one building: the first entry of buildOrder whose count it has not reached and which it can place (enough free planks and stones, a fitting spot on own land). After the food chain (pig farm, slaughterhouse) comes the big temple and the people's mana chain with a small temple; gold (Egyptians: gems too) for the combat strength comes late, where the land has it. A building that processes a mine's output (iron melt, gold melt) waits for an own mine of it or its ore on the own land (start goods). Entries that need a resource (trees, stones, ore, river, fish, swampy ground for rice) are skipped while the own land lacks it - the expansion then builds towers towards it.
_housingComment: A living house is started when fewer carriers than freeCarriers are available (residents still to come count as available), or while there are no more carriers than carriersPerProductionBuilding per production building (sites included), or when fewer than houseWhenConvertible carriers may still become specialists (recruitment.keptCarriers in production.json). Towers then leave its material.
_spareRoomComment: Living space no one needs (carriers turned soldiers): a living house that has released all its residents is torn down for its material when, without it, at least spareRoom places would still be left over and no house is wanted. The biggest such house goes first.
_foresterComment: Every checkSeconds the AI stops each forester with at least maxTrees trees (saplings too) in its work area and restarts the others.
_houseSizesComment: Which living house: the first of houseSizes whose sawmills and stonecutters (finished) the player has, otherwise house. Per people below, after what their houses cost (Egyptians build with stone, Asians and Amazons with planks).
_stockComment: A storehouse is built once a smith, gold melt or gems mine works and stockWhenWaiting units of goods worth storing (storage.materials in production.json: tools, weapons, gold, gems) lie around and the storehouses have fewer than two free piles.
_expansionComment: Towers towards what the own land lacks, in this order: quarry stone below minStoneUnits, none of the listed ores, free building land below minFreeLand, stone below wantedStoneUnits, trees below minTrees, no river (waterworks draw from rivers only); towards free land when a building found no room; with spareSoldiersForLand idle soldiers and landStock planks and stones beyond the tower's cost simply towards the nearest free land. The tower goes to the own-land spot nearest the target. While a needed tower cannot be afforded, the economy keeps its planks and stones back.

expansion._minFreeLandComment: Free building land (grass points with nothing on them and no building around) the own land should keep; below it the AI expands towards the cells with the most of it.
expansion._lateOresComment: Towers towards these only late: once every build order entry before the mine of the ore is reached (houses and the mana chain come first), after all other needs except plain land.
expansion._maxWaterShareComment: Largest share of water (sea, lakes, rivers) among the unclaimed points a tower would take. Spots with more are passed over; towards a needed resource (stone, ore, trees, water) the spot with the least water is taken if none is below.

_magicComment: Priests follow the soldiers out on a strike or campaign and stay priestDistance fields behind them (towards home); otherwise they wait at home. A priest casts its spell where own soldiers fight once the mana is there and at least minTargets soldiers would be hit (own ones for a haste spell).

magic._upgradeComment: Soldier upgrades (magic.json, upgrades) are made as soon as enough mana has been earned in all (they spend none), in upgradeOrder (all to level 2, then the same order to level 3).

military._comment: Idle soldiers outside buildings, weighed every thinkSeconds; soldiers walking on a plain move order of the AI (to a post, home) count as idle, so their order is weighed again as well. The AI knows where every enemy soldier and geologist is. Enemies within groupRadius of each other form a group (geologists do not fight: one soldier is enough against them). Guerilla comes before holding soldiers back: a group within strikeRange of an own military building is attacked by the nearest idle soldiers once they have strikeRatio times its strength (health x damage per second), also by those that would otherwise stay back against it; only soldiers needed against the other groups within threatRange (strikeRatio times their strength) are kept out. An attack on the land (enemies walking or fighting) is met anywhere; enemies just standing around only if they stand at most hinterlandDepth fields deep in their own land (0: anywhere). The other idle soldiers are placed by the character's traits (guarding): guardByThreat shares them out by how strong and close the enemy groups within threatRange are, without any threat they gather at home; frontTowers, everyOtherTower and rotatingTowers spread them over the towers while there is no threat. A soldier within guardDistance of its post stays. Without such a trait they stay where they are.

attack._comment: Campaigns against enemy land. Defence comes first: idle soldiers needed against enemies near the own land stay back, and no campaign starts while enemies stand on the own land. Target: an occupied enemy military building; its defence is its garrison plus enemy soldiers within defenseRadius. Preferred are targets close to the own land, weakly defended, with no enemy group within pathClearance of the way there. A campaign starts when the spare soldiers have ratio times the target's defence and the AI's whole army has armyRatio (default: ratio; 0: any) times that enemy's (at least minSoldiers). commit (0-1, default 0): that share of the spare soldiers left over comes along as well (1: full strength). The soldiers first gather at the own military building nearest the target (at most gatherSeconds); the campaign is given up when they then have less than abortRatio (default: ratio; 0: never) times the defence, otherwise they attack together; they retreat when they fall below military.retreatRatio (0: never), and go home when it is over. maxDistance (default 0: any): targets at most this far from the own military building nearest them.
attack._garrisonWeightComment: Per building name: its garrison counts this many times in the defence (others once). A castle's soldiers are much harder to get at (one fighter at the door, bowmen on the roofs).

_characterComment: Characters (docs/KI-TACTICS.md): traits on top of the built-in behavior, in order of priority. A character may override a trait's settings under the trait's name and any general value (after the people's), e.g. "general": { "traits": ["pincer"], "pincer": { "feintShare": 0.5 } }. buildOrderMoves (building: places, negative = earlier) shifts every entry of a building in the people's build order. Made-up characters for trying out (arena, tournament): traits joined by '+' (pincer+guardByThreat), and @path=value on top of a character or traits (general@attack.ratio=1.3@buildOrderMoves.barrack=-5). characterWeights: which character a player gets, drawn once per game (per people under civilizations). The client and the arena can name it per player with --characters.

guardByThreat._comment: Idle soldiers guard the own military buildings by threat (values under military: threatRange, guardDistance).

pincer._comment: Pincer and feint: a campaign with at least minSoldiers is split. feintShare of them gather at the own building nearest the target, the rest walk round in an arc to a staging point flankAngle degrees off that direction, flankDistance fields from the target (at least out of its bowmen's reach). When both are in place the feint attacks; strikeSeconds later the main force strikes from the side. The way round takes time: extraShare more of the spare soldiers come along, and the attack is only given up when they have become weaker than the defence (military.retreatRatio).

waves._comment: Calm phases of calmSeconds without campaigns alternate with waves of waveSeconds in which campaigns may start one after another; each phase up to jitter (share) longer or shorter. Defence and guerilla go on.

frontGarrison._comment: Military buildings within frontDistance of an enemy military building (sites too) are fully staffed, the others get backline soldiers; the rest come out and are free for strikes and campaigns.

earlyArmy._comment: The first build order entries of buildings move together, in that order, right behind the first after entries (wood and stone): the start goods (iron ore, coal) become soldiers instead of waiting for mines and food. An iron melt may be built while iron ore lies on the own land, without a mine.

frontTowers._comment: Without a threat, idle soldiers are shared out evenly among the own military buildings facing the enemy: the nearest enemy military building can be reached without a detour (the way at most detour times the straight distance plus 5 fields) and without passing another own military building. Rechecked every checkSeconds. With a threat the next trait (guardByThreat) places them.

everyOtherTower._comment: Without a threat, idle soldiers are shared out evenly among every other own military building: bigger groups, quick at the neighbors left out. Front first; a building is left out when a neighbor of it (at most neighborFactor times the distance to the nearest one) is taken. With a threat the next trait (guardByThreat) places them.

rotatingTowers._comment: Without a threat, idle soldiers are shared out evenly among a random share of the own military buildings, drawn anew every rotateSeconds. With a threat the next trait (guardByThreat) places them.

forwardBase._comment: Idle soldiers gather at the own military building nearest an enemy one, as a base for guerilla strikes. When the enemy groups within military.threatRange of it are stronger than fallBackRatio times them, they fall back (without fighting on the way) to the own military building nearest the base that lies fallBackDistance fields further from those enemies (otherwise home); an enemy moving on is fought by defence and guerilla from behind. Takes the decision point guarding: comes before guardByThreat in a character.

characters._peoplesComment: One character per people (characterWeights under civilizations), each a recognisable opponent. Egyptians (hothead): hot-tempered, military early, attack at slight superiority with all they have, thin garrisons in the back. Asians (unyielding): hardly ever give up or retreat (only below half the defence; never at all bled them out). Romans (legion): strong economy with early gold, attack bundled in waves, pincers. Amazons (skirmisher): play safe at home (garrisons full, campaigns only at 2:1), but wear the enemy down with small guerilla groups far out; campaigns only near the own land (an outpost far away is lost again). Idle soldiers without a threat: hothead keeps them in one heap at home, unyielding on a changing third of its towers, legion and general on every other tower, skirmisher on the towers facing the enemy; enemies standing around deep in their own land are left alone by the skirmisher (that mostly goes wrong).

civilizations._comment: Values per people, overriding the ones above (objects are merged). Example: "Roman": { "attack": { "ratio": 1.3 } }. Build orders per people: Romans need wood and stone alike (the general one above: one of each first, a second of each a little later); Egyptians build with much stone and little wood (one sawmill, many stonecutters); Asians and Amazons use many planks (a second wood production early, a third away from the others in long games; one stonecutter at first).
